objects.value: Initial Veterinary Examination and Health Assessment
Core Vaccinations (often given in a series of boosters)
First Vaccination Dose (typically around 6-8 weeks of age for puppies and kittens)
Second Vaccination Dose (usually 3-4 weeks after the first)
Third Vaccination Dose (if needed, often 3-4 weeks after the second)
Rabies Vaccination (timing varies by location and vaccine)
Booster Vaccinations (given periodically throughout the pet's life)
Optional or Non-Core Vaccinations (if recommended based on risk)
Titre Testing (in some cases, to assess immunity levels instead of routine boosters)
Vaccination Record Keeping
Discussion of Potential Side Effects
Monitoring After Vaccination
Legal Requirements Review (for rabies and other vaccines)
Travel Vaccination Considerations (if applicable)
Bordetella Vaccination (often required for boarding or grooming)
Influenza Vaccination (for dogs and sometimes cats)
Lyme Disease Vaccination (in endemic areas)
Feline Leukemia Virus (FeLV) Vaccination (for cats at risk)
Feline Immunodeficiency Virus (FIV) Vaccination (for cats at risk - efficacy debated)
Canine Parainfluenza Virus Vaccination (often in combination vaccines)
Leptospirosis Vaccination (for dogs at risk)
Coronavirus Vaccination (for dogs, not the same as human COVID-19)
Giardia Vaccination (for dogs, efficacy debated)
Regular Veterinary Check-ups to Review Vaccination Needs
